title: The 2014 Algorithm Invoice
subtitle: Southern Trust · Estate Planning · Documentary Boundaries
description: A 2013 revised estate-planning service-letter draft and a 2014 Southern Trust algorithm invoice document are compared as separate records with overlapping counterparties. Neither establishes completed payment, software delivery or an amendment linking them.

sources.title: Southern Trust algorithms invoice document
sources.note: One-page Southern Trust invoice addressed to Leon Black, containing an unfilled bracketed entity placeholder. It describes $20 million in estate-planning-related algorithms. Does not by itself establish settlement, delivery, or actual system operation. Avoid reproducing banking details.

sources.title: Revised draft estate-planning service letter
sources.note: Archive-indexed February 11, 2013; header identifies February 6 revisions to a February 5 lawyer's draft. Draft terms describe a conditional $23.5 million estate-planning fee to Southern Trust. Does not establish execution, payment, algorithm development, or relation to the July 2014 invoice.

hypotheses.question: Was the stated algorithm service actually delivered or paid for?
hypotheses.context: The document identifies an amount and a broad service description but does not show implementation or payment.
hypotheses.forEvidence: An invoice document exists identifying parties and a service category.
hypotheses.againstEvidence: A bracketed placeholder and lack of payment confirmation, agreement scope, code records, or delivery acceptance prevent a definitive operational conclusion.
hypotheses.nextCheck: Locate the signed agreement, final recipient entity, invoice settlement record, work product, and independent service delivery evidence.

hypotheses.question: Did the 2013 draft and 2014 algorithm invoice refer to the same engagement?
hypotheses.context: Both name Southern Trust and Leon Black in an estate-planning context, but their amounts, dates and documentary forms differ.
hypotheses.forEvidence: The same broad counterparties and estate-planning subject occur in a 2013 draft and a 2014 invoice document.
hypotheses.againstEvidence: A revised unsigned draft cannot establish a finalized 2013 contract, and the 2014 invoice retains an unfinished entity placeholder. No explicit amendment or cross-reference has been identified.
hypotheses.nextCheck: Find a fully executed agreement, amendment, final invoice and payment records explicitly linking the terms. Do not add their dollar amounts together.

traceSteps.notEstablished: Whether the draft was executed, any money was settled, software was produced, or it constituted the same agreement as the July 2014 algorithms invoice.
